input: Given /data/team_a.txt and /data/team_b.txt containing member names (one per line, already sorted), use the comm command to find: 1) Members only in Team A (print under 'Only Team A:'). 2) Members only in Team B (print under 'Only Team B:'). 3) Members in both teams (print under 'Both teams:'). Print the count of each group.

transcript.final_response:
I ran `comm` on the two sorted files, using `-23`, `-13` and `-12` to pick out each group.

**Only Team A:**
- alice
- dave
- eve

**Only Team B:**
- frank
- grace

**Both teams:**
- bob
- carol

**Counts:**
- Only Team A: 3
- Only Team B: 2
- Both teams: 2
tool_calls: cd /data; echo "Only Team A:"; comm -23 team_a.txt team_b.txt | tee /tmp/a; echo "Only Team B:"; comm -13 team_a.txt team_b.txt | tee /tmp/b; echo "Both teams:"; comm -12 team_a.txt team_b.txt | tee /tmp/c; echo; echo "Counts: Only A=$(wc -l </tmp/a) Only B=$(wc -l </tmp/b) Both=$(wc -l </tmp/c)"
